teachBack.text: You open each invoice and compare the line category with the pre-coded cost center. If they match, you leave the coding alone and post it, because touching correct coding is wasted work. For equipment over €5,000 gross, you recode it to CapEx cost center 0400, since it's an asset, not maintenance. You only book it there with an asset number. For any group subsidiary like Keller CZ, you get a second approval from the controller, currently Dr. Fisher, before posting. That applies whatever the amount, even below the usual €10,000 threshold. In December, especially with Nordlicht, you check the supplier's history. An identical amount means a duplicate, so you hold it, note which invoice it repeats, and ask for a credit note. Did I get that right?

workMap.summary: Thomas Brandt opens each incoming invoice and checks whether the pre-coded cost center matches the line category. He only changes the coding when it doesn't match. Equipment over €5,000 gross is recoded to CapEx cost center 0400, and he books it there only if it has an asset number. Every invoice from a group subsidiary, such as Keller CZ, goes to the controller (currently Dr. Fisher) for a second approval before posting, whatever the amount. In December he checks supplier history for double billing: an invoice with the same amount as an earlier one is a duplicate, so he puts it on hold and asks the supplier for a credit note.

pages.title: If the pre-coded cost center fits the line category, leave the coding as is
pages.situation: An invoice arrives already pre-coded, and the cost center matches what the lines are (for example freight on 4800). The expert does not touch the coding and posts it. He only recodes when the category and cost center don't fit.
pages.triggerText: When an invoice's pre-coded cost center already matches its line category

recognize.text: Invoice already shows a cost center
The line category matches that cost center (e.g. freight → 4800, material → maintenance 4711)

steps.text: Open the invoice and compare the line category with the pre-coded cost center.
If they match, leave the coding unchanged. Only use set_invoice_coding when it doesn't fit.

why.text: Recoding is only needed when the pre-coding is wrong. Touching correct coding is extra work with no benefit.
